method.order: Alternating before/after and after/before in fresh CLI processes, without concurrent test workloads.
method.database: In-memory DuckDB database; grouped states can spill to a temporary directory.
method.timing: DuckDB JSON profile query.total_time for CREATE TABLE f AS only.
method.rss: macOS /usr/bin/time -l maximum resident set size, whole process, bytes; not DuckDB managed memory.
method.reproduction: Load the corresponding extension in build/release/duckdb -unsigned -json, apply settings, enable JSON profiling, execute each case SQL, then disable profiling and read sum(octet_length(f)), sum(bitfilter_info(f).entries) from f.
notes: Only the duplicate sampling implementation differs between the two extension builds.
The sample uses the same 4096-element stack buffer; positions are deduplicated before keys are fetched, so unique input cannot trigger deduplication by sampling a row twice.
Input-wide deduplication still materializes and sorts a full key copy; this can increase build time and peak RSS.
Sampling remains a heuristic; single-group input collection is unchanged.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT k >> 61 AS part, binary_fuse8_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, (hash(i % 80000) & 9223372036854775807::UBIGINT) << 1 AS k FROM range(8000000) t(i)) GROUP BY part;
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT 0 AS part, binary_fuse8_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(8000000) t(i));
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT k >> 61 AS part, binary_fuse8_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(8000000) t(i)) GROUP BY part;
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT i % 64 AS part, binary_fuse8_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(1048576) t(i)) GROUP BY part;
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT 0 AS part, xor8_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(2000000) t(i));
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT 0 AS part, xor16_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(2000000) t(i));
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT 0 AS part, binary_fuse8_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(2000000) t(i));
CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT 0 AS part, binary_fuse16_filter(k) AS f FROM (SELECT i, hash(i) AS k FROM range(2000000) t(i));

duplicate_membership_checks.method: Existing benchmark_fuse_partitions.py --workload duplicate --parts 8 --memory 64MB --trials 3 --probes, once per extension build. These probe runs use persisted databases. All 8000000 source rows tested each trial, plus 2000000 guaranteed-absent odd keys. Present-phase matches count false negatives.
